data.gender_notes: Adina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Adina is derived from the Hebrew word 'adan', which means 'to adorn'. It was a common name in ancient Israel and is mentioned several times in the Old Testament. The name symbolizes beauty, delight, and adornment. In the Book of Numbers (26:33), Adina is mentioned as the name of a daughter of the tribe of Dan. In the Book of Judges (5:12), Adina is mentioned as one of the names given to the newborn son of Jabin, King of Canaan, after his mother was defeated by Deborah and Barak. In Christian tradition, Adina represents the grace and beauty of the Lord, as well as the adornment of virtue and good works.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's grace and beauty.
data.etymology: Adina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Adornment, Delight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adina total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: עדינה
in_hebrew.meaning: אשה חזקה ועדינה, סמל של חולשה רבה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עדינה היא שם נשי המקור בעברית, ומשמעותו 'אשה חזקה ועדינה, סמל של חולשה רבה' . נראה כי שם זה מוזכר בספר שופטים 14:6 כשם אדם, ופירושו 'מסולף, חלש.' בגדולים, שם זה מסמל חולשה ודעת הכלה. כיום, שם זה נפוץ בעולם הנוצרי כשם נשי נפרד, ומשמעותו 'אשה חזקה ועדינה'.

in_greek.name: Άδυνα
in_greek.meaning: καταπληκτική και αισθητή, έμφαση στην ευλυμία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Άδυνα προέρχεται από το ελληνικό Άδυνατος, το οποίο σημαίνει 'απίθανος' ή 'καταπληκτικός'. Στη Βίβλο, το όνομα αυτό δεν εντοπίζεται, αλλά το συναφές όνομα Άδυνατος εμφανίζεται ως χαρακτηρισμός για τον Μωσαϊκό. Στη μεσαιωνική εποχή, το όνομα Άδυνα χρησιμοποιήθηκε ως τίτλος για τον Ιησού. Σήμερα, το όνομα Άδυνα χρησιμοποιείται ως τίτλος για γυναίκες και δίνει έμφαση στην ευλυμία και την απρόσμενη εμφάνιση.

in_latin.name: Adina
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Adina originem habet a verbo Graeco, quod significat 'gentilis, delicatus, rarus'. Non in Sacris Scripturis sed in historia Christiana mentionem habet. In mediis aevi, nomen Adina ut titulus utilis erat. Hodie, nomen Adina ut nomen femininum utilis est, significans 'dulcis, delicatus, rarius'.

historical_references.reference: Adina, a biblical name, is mentioned in the Old Testament book of Samuel (2 Samuel 2:13-14). In this context, Adina is the name of a concubine of King Saul, who was given to his son, Ish-bosheth, to be his wife. When Ish-bosheth's rival, David, heard that Adina had made David's son, Amnon, dance before her naked, he sent a party to kill him in a rage.

Adina, a Christian saint, was a martyr in Egypt in the 4th century. Her story is told in the Golden Legend. Adina was a beautiful virgin who was accused of helping a pagan man escape from prison. She was tortured and killed, but she remained steadfast in her faith and was eventually beheaded.
